sources.entry: Ganymede ⚠ - Twitch VOD and live stream archiving platform. Includes a rendered chat for each archive. GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Ganymede is a self-hosted Twitch VOD and live stream archiving platform that records streams with real-time chat playback and a rendered chat file for each archive.
summary.what_it_does: Ganymede archives past Twitch broadcasts (VODs) and live streams, saving them with a rendered chat for each archive that can be viewed outside Ganymede. Files are stored in a simple folder structure intended to remain usable without the app. The web UI offers real-time chat playback, playlists, playback progress saving, and light/dark mode. A "watched channels" feature automatically archives channels with advanced filtering options. It also supports a recoverable queue, custom FFmpeg parameters for post-download video, custom chat render parameters, webhook notifications, SSO/OAuth login, and an API documented in the docs folder. It runs as two Docker containers: the server and a Postgres database.
use_cases: archive Twitch VODs and live streams
keep long-term copies of past streams
how_to_run: Download a copy of the docker-compose.yml file.
Edit docker-compose.yml to set environment variables (Twitch client ID and secret, database settings, volume paths).
Visit the frontend address and port, log in as admin with password ganymede, then change the admin password or create a new admin user and delete the default one.
notable: Renders chat into a file saved with each archive, so it can be viewed without Ganymede
Simple file structure meant to outlast the application
Watched channels with filtering for automatic archiving of live and past broadcasts
Recoverable queue and temp files mounted to host for crash recovery
caveats: Requires a Twitch application client ID and secret, and a Linux environment with Docker
Needs 50GB+ free storage, and chat downloads use about 1.9GB of memory per execution
Default admin credentials must be changed after first login
